Uploads an image you have locally (a file in your workspace, a sandbox attachment) when it can’t be provided otherwise: it has no internet address and your environment can’t connect to the database. The file goes in base64 chunks in consecutive calls of this tool, and the connector assembles it on its side. Every byte passes through the conversation, so this is a way for graphics up to a few hundred KB.
Steps:
1. step="start": name (with extension), size (bytes), sha256 (SHA-256 of the content, 64 hex characters), chunk_size (bytes, 16384 to 524288; recommended 49152), optionally width_px, height_px, replace (id or name of the image to replace – pages show the new file right away). Result: upload id and number of chunks. If the same file is already in the project, the result says so right away.
2. step="part": upload_id, index (from 0), data_base64 – the bytes from index×chunk_size, of length chunk_size (the last one shorter). Any order; a repeat replaces.
3. step="finish": upload_id – checks completeness and size; the image goes to the project images. Missing chunks are listed.
Unpack a ZIP locally and upload the images one by one. An upload not finished within a day is removed.

start: wielkość kawałka w bajtach (16384: start: chunk size in bytes (16384–524288, default 49152)
